method: API gravity is a density scale for petroleum liquids: API = 141.5 / SG − 131.5, where SG is the oil's specific gravity at 60 °F (15.56 °C) relative to water at the same temperature, so SG = 141.5 / (API + 131.5). This page accepts whichever of the three measures you already have — API gravity, specific gravity or density in kg/m³ — converts it to the other two and shows the density in kg/m³, lb/ft³ and kg/L. For the volume-to-mass step it treats water at 60 °F as 999.016 kg/m³, the ASTM D1250 (2008) value, and a barrel as 42 US gallons, 0.158987294928 m³, so a metric tonne of oil occupies 1,000 / (density × 0.158987294928) barrels; at 35 °API that is 849.0 kg/m³ and 7.408 barrels per tonne. Grades follow the common cut-offs: light above 31.1 °API, medium from 22.3 to 31.1, heavy below 22.3 and extra heavy below 10. Inputs are limited to -10 to 150 °API, 0.3 to 2.5 specific gravity or 300 to 2500 kg/m³. No temperature correction is applied: a hydrometer or densimeter reading taken at another temperature must first be corrected to 60 °F with the ASTM D1250 tables. Everything is computed in the browser and nothing is uploaded.

sources.title: API gravity — Wikipedia: gives API = 141.5/SG − 131.5 and its inverse, the 2008 ASTM D1250 water density of 999.016 kg/m³ at 60 °F, barrels per metric tonne as (API + 131.5)/(141.5 × 0.159), and the light above 31.1, medium 22.3–31.1, heavy below 22.3 and extra-heavy below 10 °API grades
U.S. Energy Information Administration glossary, barrel: a unit of volume equal to 42 U.S. gallons
